question: True or false: a US infant vaccine was withdrawn about a year after licensing over a rare complication confirmed only after launch?
answer: True. RotaShield, a rotavirus vaccine licensed in 1998, was pulled in 1999 after reports of intussusception, a telescoping of the bowel, reached a national reporting system. The excess risk was on the order of 1 in 10,000 infants. Trials of about 10,000 children could not reliably see so rare an event; mass use could.
move: A study cannot see an event much rarer than one in its sample size.
ask: What event am I declaring safe from a sample too small to ever have seen it?
trap: Assuming a licensed vaccine's trials would have caught any serious harm.
reference: Murphy et al., Intussusception among infants given an oral rotavirus vaccine, New England Journal of Medicine, 2001
